subject: Cross-region failover: customer impact summary and next steps
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 08:14:22 -0700
Subject: [SEV-1] AtlasFin: cross-region failover causing elevated tail latency

Team — forwarding the PagerDuty alert I picked up from the monitoring channel. Atlas Financial (production) experienced an automatic cross-region failover at 07:58 PT. Symptoms observed: sustained 95th/99th percentile token latency spikes for interactive generation routes and a small increase in error rate on the long-poll streaming endpoints.

What I have so far:
- PagerDuty incident PD-78291 (linked).
- Failover triggered due to transient packet loss between us-east-1 and us-west-2; control-plane confirmed the region switch but routing back to primary did not complete cleanly for a subset of their sessions.
- Impact window started ~07:58, initial mitigation steps (prefix cache warm, route reestablished) were attempted but not fully restoring 99th pct by 08:05.

Immediate asks:
1) Lauren — can you triage kernel-level logs for the serving nodes assigned to AtlasFin (dedicated pool) and confirm whether KV cache rebuilds stalled?
2) Ben — need an executive-facing one-paragraph note for AtlasFin (Sean) saying we’re on it and committing to a 30-min follow-up with timeline.
3) Evelyn — please prepare to coordinate customer comms and handle any SLA inquiries.

I attached a short timeline CSV as I compile events. I’ll stay on the PD bridge and update.

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 08:28:46 -0700
Subject: Re: [SEV-1] AtlasFin: cross-region failover causing elevated tail latency

Diego / Ben — quick update from infra:
- Confirmed that two serving racks in us-east-1 experienced rapid socket resets during the failover window; KV cache rebuild daemons restarted but backlog of cache restores hit CPU scheduling thrash on the primary hosts.
- We isolated the nodes and applied a targeted process restart (hotfix-rollback.patch attached) to clear the rebuild queue. Initial metrics show 95th percentile latency returning toward baseline as of 08:25.
- No data loss; only request latency and a handful of 502-level errors during the storm.

Next steps I’m executing now:
- Keep the impacted rack in isolated mode for 20 more minutes to monitor stability.
- Collect per-session logs for a sample of affected requests and hand off to Diego for deeper KV cache correlation.

Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean O'Neal <sean@atlasfin.com>, Infra Support <infra-support@atlasfin.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 08:37:10 -0700
Subject: Atlas Financial — immediate update on production impact (follow-up in 30m)

Sean — I’m Ben from the Redwood Inference team supporting Atlas Financial. We detected an automated cross-region failover this morning at ~07:58 PT which temporarily increased tail latencies on your interactive generation endpoints. Our engineers are actively mitigating and we’ve begun applying a targeted rollback on a small subset of serving nodes that were rebuilding KV caches.

What we are doing now:
- Confirming stability on affected racks and monitoring your request latency in 5-minute windows.
- Collecting logs to determine why some sessions did not gracefully route back to primary after failover.

Commitment: we’ll provide a follow-up update in ~30 minutes with an expected time-to-restoration estimate and any actions you should take. We will also share a concise post-incident note and timeline when we have it.

If you prefer a quick bridge instead of email, let me know and I’ll have an invite out immediately.

— Ben Carter
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwoodinference.com>, Sean O'Neal <sean@atlasfin.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 09:02:58 -0700
Subject: Re: Atlas Financial — immediate update on production impact (follow-up in 30m)

Sean / all — quick engineering snapshot:
- Correlated traces show that sessions routed through the affected edge nodes had KV cache misses that triggered large synchronous disk reads while the cache rebuild was in progress. Those synchronous operations are the primary root cause for the 99th percentile latency spikes.
- Action taken: isolated the hot processes and staged the hotfix (attached) that forces asynchronous cache warmup and avoids blocking request threads during rebuilds. Metrics are improving; 95th pct is back to normal, 99th pct has improved ~60% compared to peak.

Short-term recommendation for AtlasFin: there is no customer action required. If you saw client-visible failures, they were transient and we don’t expect replay. We will deliver a formal post-incident summary within 48 hours and follow up on any SLA impacts.

Diego
SRE, Redwood Inference

Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwoodinference.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 12:03:10 -0700
Subject: AtlasFin post-incident snapshot and next steps

Sean — follow-up from this morning’s event: thanks for your patience. Attaching a short executive summary PDF and the timeline CSV. Key takeaways:
- Root cause: KV cache rebuilds on a serving rack overwhelmed CPU scheduling after an automated cross-region failover; synchronous cache fill behavior amplified tail latency for a subset of sessions.
- Impact window: ~07:58 - 08:30 PT for affected traffic; most traffic restored to baseline by 08:25 after targeted process restarts and the staged async warmup patch.
- Customer-visible effects: elevated 95th/99th pct token latency and some 502 errors; no data loss or model-state corruption.

Planned follow-ups we will deliver in the next 48 hours:
1) A 1-page engineering postmortem with action items and timelines (link to draft).
2) An ops change to make cache warmup asynchronous across serving racks (ETA: 2 weeks).
3) A runbook improvement and additional probe coverage to detect similar failover-induced cache storms (ETA: 1 week for probe, 3 weeks for runbook rollout).

If you’d like a live 15-minute sync to walk through the timeline, happy to host.

— Ben Carter
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
